change_summary: The article has been withdrawn at the editor's request, and its full text and PDF were replaced by a withdrawal statement. The statement says the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The stored version's main results (peak indoor temperature difference and hours above threshold) are indoor temperature results, so they fall under this statement.
evaluation: Your draft cites Okafor et al. [14] in Section 2.2 and the Discussion for the 2.1 °C reduction in peak indoor temperature, which it uses as the green-roof parameter in its model. The article has been withdrawn, and the withdrawal statement says the indoor temperature records were processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. The 2.1 °C figure is one of those results, so the main green-roof estimate in your Results and Conclusions rests on a value that is now unreliable. This matters a great deal for the draft.
recommendation: Stop and raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, because your model's green-roof parameter is the 2.1 °C value from an article that has been withdrawn, and the withdrawal statement says its indoor temperature records had an incorrect sensor calibration, so the reported results cannot be relied on. Then replace or remove the citation in the Discussion and re-check the claims that scale with that value.
